judgements.justification: A's 3GRx proposed STOC/FOCS/COLT, AuTG called the result 'somewhat niche', and the AC chose a poster for 'a handful of experts'; no B reviewer raised breadth.
No reviewer misread the paper as a detractor; A's lowest scores are 6s on significance, and A's chair did not argue acceptance against a low score.
The paper is theory and neither forum got new experiments or analyses; both rebuttals gave the same concessions and assertions.
A's most expert review, AuTG at confidence 4, gave 6, which is not above its less-informed reviewers (UuHj gave 7).
No score changed after the response period; AuTG's 'somewhat niche' came with an unchanged score, and px8j's late edit raised the score after answers.
A's 6s came with stated reservations on audience, gain size and novelty, so the gap reflects a different judgement, not a leniency of scale.
No reviewer or chair in either committee called the headline claim or title overstated.
A's 6s rested on stated significance and audience objections, including the expert AuTG's, not on reviewers unable to check the technical core.
